paragraphs.text: translated by
1. YOUR radiant Chariot-whither goes it on its way?-who decks it for you, Heroes, for its happy course,
paragraphs.original: रथं यान्तं कुह को ह वां नरा प्रति द्युमन्तं सुविताय भूषति ।
paragraphs.translit: rathaṃ yāntaṃ kuha ko ha vāṃ narā prati dyumantaṃ suvitāya bhūṣati |

paragraphs.text: Starting at daybreak, visiting each morning every house, borne hitherward through prayer unto the sacrifice?
paragraphs.original: प्रातर्यावाणं विभ्वं विशेविशे वस्तोर्वस्तोर्वहमानं धिया शमि
paragraphs.translit: prātaryāvāṇaṃ vibhvaṃ viśeviśe vastorvastorvahamānaṃ dhiyā śami

paragraphs.text: 2. Where are ye, Asvins, in the evening, where at morn? Where is your halting place, where rest ye for the night?
paragraphs.original: कुह स्विद्दोषा कुह वस्तोरश्विना कुहाभिपित्वं करतः कुहोषतुः ।
paragraphs.translit: kuha sviddoṣā kuha vastoraśvinā kuhābhipitvaṃ karataḥ kuhoṣatuḥ |

paragraphs.text: Who brings you homeward, as the widow bed ward draws her husband's brother, as the bride attracts the groom?
paragraphs.original: को वां शयुत्रा विधवेव देवरं मर्यं न योषा कृणुते सधस्थ आ
paragraphs.translit: ko vāṃ śayutrā vidhaveva devaraṃ maryaṃ na yoṣā kṛṇute sadhastha ā

paragraphs.text: 3. Early ye sing forth praise as with a herald's voice, and, meet for worship, go each morning to the house.
paragraphs.original: प्रातर्जरेथे जरणेव कापया वस्तोर्वस्तोर्यजता गच्छथो गृहम् ।
paragraphs.translit: prātarjarethe jaraṇeva kāpayā vastorvastoryajatā gacchatho gṛham |

paragraphs.text: Whom do ye ever bring to ruin? Unto whose libations come ye, Heroes, like two Sons of Kings?
paragraphs.original: कस्य ध्वस्रा भवथः कस्य वा नरा राजपुत्रेव सवनाव गच्छथः
paragraphs.translit: kasya dhvasrā bhavathaḥ kasya vā narā rājaputreva savanāva gacchathaḥ

paragraphs.text: 4. Even as hunters follow two wild elephants, we with oblations call you down at morn and eve.
paragraphs.original: युवां मृगेव वारणा मृगण्यवो दोषा वस्तोर्हविषा नि ह्वयामहे ।
paragraphs.translit: yuvāṃ mṛgeva vāraṇā mṛgaṇyavo doṣā vastorhaviṣā ni hvayāmahe |

paragraphs.text: To folk who pay you offierings at appointed times, Chiefs, Lords of splendour, ye bring food to strengthen them.
paragraphs.original: युवं होत्रामृतुथा जुह्वते नरेषं जनाय वहथः शुभस्पती
paragraphs.translit: yuvaṃ hotrāmṛtuthā juhvate nareṣaṃ janāya vahathaḥ śubhaspatī

paragraphs.text: 5. To you, O Asvins, came the daughter of a King, Ghosa, and said, O Heroes, this I beg of you:
paragraphs.original: युवां ह घोषा पर्यश्विना यती राज्ञ ऊचे दुहिता पृच्छे वां नरा ।
paragraphs.translit: yuvāṃ ha ghoṣā paryaśvinā yatī rājña ūce duhitā pṛcche vāṃ narā |

paragraphs.text: Be near me in the day, he near me in the night: help me to gain a car-borne chieftain rich in steeds.
paragraphs.original: भूतं मे अह्न उत भूतमक्तवेऽश्वावते रथिने शक्तमर्वते
paragraphs.translit: bhūtaṃ me ahna uta bhūtamaktave'śvāvate rathine śaktamarvate

paragraphs.text: 6. O Asvins, ye are wise: as Kutsa comes to men, bring your car nigh the folk of him who sings your praise.
paragraphs.original: युवं कवी ष्ठः पर्यश्विना रथं विशो न कुत्सो जरितुर्नशायथः ।
paragraphs.translit: yuvaṃ kavī ṣṭhaḥ paryaśvinā rathaṃ viśo na kutso jariturnaśāyathaḥ |

paragraphs.text: The bee, O Asvins, bears your honey in her mouth, as the maid carries it purified in her hand.
paragraphs.original: युवोर्ह मक्षा पर्यश्विना मध्वासा भरत निष्कृतं न योषणा
paragraphs.translit: yuvorha makṣā paryaśvinā madhvāsā bharata niṣkṛtaṃ na yoṣaṇā

paragraphs.text: 7. To Bhujyu and to Vasa ye come near with help, O Asvins, to Sinjara and to Usana.
paragraphs.original: युवं ह भुज्युं युवमश्विना वशं युवं शिञ्जारमुशनामुपारथुः ।
paragraphs.translit: yuvaṃ ha bhujyuṃ yuvamaśvinā vaśaṃ yuvaṃ śiñjāramuśanāmupārathuḥ |

paragraphs.text: Your worshipper secures your friendship for himself. Through your protection I desire felicity.
paragraphs.original: युवो ररावा परि सख्यमासते युवोरहमवसा सुम्नमा चके
paragraphs.translit: yuvo rarāvā pari sakhyamāsate yuvorahamavasā sumnamā cake

paragraphs.text: 8. Krsa and Sayu ye protect, ye Asvins Twain: ye Two assist the widow and the worshipper;
paragraphs.original: युवं ह कृशं युवमश्विना शयुं युवं विधन्तं विधवामुरुष्यथः ।
paragraphs.translit: yuvaṃ ha kṛśaṃ yuvamaśvinā śayuṃ yuvaṃ vidhantaṃ vidhavāmuruṣyathaḥ |

paragraphs.text: And ye throw open, Asvins, unto those who win the cattle-stall that thunders with its serenfold mouth.
paragraphs.original: युवं सनिभ्य स्तनयन्तमश्विनाप व्रजमूर्णुथः सप्तास्यम्
paragraphs.translit: yuvaṃ sanibhya stanayantamaśvināpa vrajamūrṇuthaḥ saptāsyam

paragraphs.text: 9. The Woman hath brought forth, the Infant hath appeared, the plants of wondrous beauty straightway have sprung up.
paragraphs.original: जनिष्ट योषा पतयत्कनीनको वि चारुहन्वीरुधो दंसना अनु ।
paragraphs.translit: janiṣṭa yoṣā patayatkanīnako vi cāruhanvīrudho daṃsanā anu |

paragraphs.text: To him the rivers run as down a deep descent, and he this day becomes their master and their lord.
paragraphs.original: आस्मै रीयन्ते निवनेव सिन्धवोऽस्मा अह्ने भवति तत्पतित्वनम्
paragraphs.translit: āsmai rīyante nivaneva sindhavo'smā ahne bhavati tatpatitvanam

paragraphs.text: 10. They mourn the living, cry aloud, at sacrifice: the men have set their thoughts upon a distant cast.
paragraphs.original: जीवं रुदन्ति वि मयन्ते अध्वरे दीर्घामनु प्रसितिं दीधियुर्नरः ।
paragraphs.translit: jīvaṃ rudanti vi mayante adhvare dīrghāmanu prasitiṃ dīdhiyurnaraḥ |

paragraphs.text: A lovely thing for fathers who have gathered here,-a joy to husbands,-are the wives their arms shall clasp
paragraphs.original: वामं पितृभ्यो य इदं समेरिरे मयः पतिभ्यो जनयः परिष्वजे
paragraphs.translit: vāmaṃ pitṛbhyo ya idaṃ samerire mayaḥ patibhyo janayaḥ pariṣvaje

paragraphs.text: 11. Of this we have no knowledge. Tall it forth to us, now the youth rests within the chambers of the bride.
paragraphs.original: न तस्य विद्म तदु षु प्र वोचत युवा ह यद्युवत्याः क्षेति योनिषु ।
paragraphs.translit: na tasya vidma tadu ṣu pra vocata yuvā ha yadyuvatyāḥ kṣeti yoniṣu |

paragraphs.text: Fain would we reach the dwelling of the vigorous Steer who loves the kine, O Asvins: this is our desire.
paragraphs.original: प्रियोस्रियस्य वृषभस्य रेतिनो गृहं गमेमाश्विना तदुश्मसि
paragraphs.translit: priyosriyasya vṛṣabhasya retino gṛhaṃ gamemāśvinā taduśmasi

paragraphs.text: 12. Your favouring grace hath come, ye Lords of ample wealth: Asvins, our longings are stored up within your hearts.
paragraphs.original: आ वामगन्सुमतिर्वाजिनीवसू न्यश्विना हृत्सु कामा अयंसत ।
paragraphs.translit: ā vāmagansumatirvājinīvasū nyaśvinā hṛtsu kāmā ayaṃsata |

paragraphs.text: Ye, Lords of splendour, have become our twofold guard: may we as welcome friends reach Aryaman's abode.
paragraphs.original: अभूतं गोपा मिथुना शुभस्पती प्रिया अर्यम्णो दुर्याँ अशीमहि
paragraphs.translit: abhūtaṃ gopā mithunā śubhaspatī priyā aryamṇo duryām̐ aśīmahi

paragraphs.text: 13. Even so, rejoicing in the dwelling-place of man, give hero sons and riches to the eloquent.
paragraphs.original: ता मन्दसाना मनुषो दुरोण आ धत्तं रयिं सहवीरं वचस्यवे ।
paragraphs.translit: tā mandasānā manuṣo duroṇa ā dhattaṃ rayiṃ sahavīraṃ vacasyave |

paragraphs.text: Make a ford, Lords of splendour, where men well may drink: remove the spiteful tree-stump standing in the path.
paragraphs.original: कृतं तीर्थं सुप्रपाणं शुभस्पती स्थाणुं पथेष्ठामप दुर्मतिं हतम्
paragraphs.translit: kṛtaṃ tīrthaṃ suprapāṇaṃ śubhaspatī sthāṇuṃ patheṣṭhāmapa durmatiṃ hatam

paragraphs.text: 14. O Asvins, Wonder-Workers, Lords of lustre, where and with what folk do ye delight yourselves to-day?
paragraphs.original: क्व स्विदद्य कतमास्वश्विना विक्षु दस्रा मादयेते शुभस्पती ।
paragraphs.translit: kva svidadya katamāsvaśvinā vikṣu dasrā mādayete śubhaspatī |

paragraphs.text: Who hath detained them with him? Whither are they gone? Unto what sage's or what worshipper's abode?
paragraphs.original: क ईं नि येमे कतमस्य जग्मतुर्विप्रस्य वा यजमानस्य वा गृहम्
paragraphs.translit: ka īṃ ni yeme katamasya jagmaturviprasya vā yajamānasya vā gṛham
